title: The 30th of September
subject: One picture, every reason to celebrate
blurb: Every one of these is a real thing somebody celebrates on the 30th of September - and some of them are birthdays. They are all in the picture. Name the missing word in each.

items.spot: A globe with two speech bubbles above it, one white and one yellow.
items.hint: Eleven letters. Turning one language into another, on the feast day of the man who did it to the Bible.

items.template: ___ Shirt Day, Canada's National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
items.hint: Six letters, and a colour. A girl's new shirt was taken from her on her first day at residential school.
items.note: For Phyllis Webstad, whose shirt it was.

items.spot: Three sticks of gum standing side by side, the middle one unwrapped.
items.hint: Three letters. You are not supposed to swallow it.

items.template: Born today in 1861: William ___ Jr, who built an empire on chewing gum
items.spot: A baseball, with ivy growing along the bottom of the frame.
items.hint: Seven letters. He started out selling soap and gave gum away as a free gift; the gift outsold the soap. A Chicago ballpark carries his name.
items.note: Sharing the day with National Chewing Gum Day is a coincidence, but a good one.

items.template: Born today in 1924: Truman ___, who wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's
items.spot: A typewriter with a sheet of paper in it.
items.hint: Six letters. His In Cold Blood more or less invented the true crime book.

items.template: St ___, patron saint of translators, who is always painted with a lion
items.spot: A lion's face, mane and all.
items.hint: Six letters. He translated the Bible into Latin, and legend says he pulled a thorn from a lion's paw.
items.note: Today is his feast day, which is why the translators have it.

items.spot: A studio microphone on a stand, with sound waves either side.
items.hint: Seven letters. Everyone you know has thought about starting one.

items.template: Born today in 1832: Ann ___, whose daughter founded Mother's Day in her memory
items.hint: Six letters. Her daughter Anna chose the white carnation as the flower of the day.
items.note: Anna later campaigned against what the day had become.

items.template: Born today in 1957: Fran ___, star of The Nanny
items.spot: A pram, seen from the side.
items.hint: Eight letters. The voice is the most recognisable thing about her, and she knows it.
items.note: She later led the Screen Actors Guild through its 2023 strike.

items.template: Born today in 1931: Angie ___, who starred in Police Woman
items.spot: A police light bar, red and blue, above a windscreen.
items.hint: Nine letters. Her series was the first American cop show built around a woman, and it shares a surname with a famous poet.
items.note: She was also in the original Ocean's Eleven.

items.spot: A blue flag with a black stripe edged in white, on a pole.
items.hint: Eight letters. A southern African country whose flag puts water first: blue for rain in a dry land.
items.note: Called Boipuso, meaning self-rule. Diamonds were found at Orapa the following year.

items.spot: A large red heart with two small figures below it.
items.hint: Six letters. The other ones. All of them.
